lines.text: Now the real Java. Every line number shown is the real one.
Lines one to eighteen: licence and imports, the tools this file borrows.
Lines twenty to thirty-three, the Javadoc: our four questions, written down.
Line thirty-four extends Classic Command: initialize once, then execute and is finished every loop, then end.
Lines thirty-five and thirty-six warn: plan to brake below the limiter's limits, or it overshoots.
Line thirty-seven, max speed: four meters per second, about eighty-eight percent of free speed.
Line thirty-eight, decel: six. Braking harder costs tag accuracy, says the comment.
Line forty, K P: six. Line forty-two, reaction time: zero point zero five seconds; zero point one zero with slower odometry.
Line forty-three, stop deadband: three millimeters.
Lines forty-five to fifty, heading: six, six, five, zero point zero five, and zero point three degrees.
Line fifty-four, max switch radius: zero point four meters. Line fifty-six, settled speed: five centimeters per second.
Distances green, speeds blue, accelerations orange, angles purple, times yellow. Same colours as the board.
